title_clean: The Six Sets of Six — Mahāṣaṣṭhāna Sutta (MN 148)
description_short: Bhante Bodhidhamma explores the Great Sixfold Base discourse, revealing how the six senses lead either to suffering through indulgence or to liberation through Right Awareness.
description_long:
In this comprehensive teaching, Bhante Bodhidhamma examines the Mahāṣaṣṭhāna Sutta (MN 148), known as the discourse on the Great Sixfold Base. This sutta serves as a masterful revision of core Buddhist teachings, demonstrating how all aspects of the Dhamma interconnect through the mechanism of the six sense bases.

The talk explores how contact through the six senses (eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind) becomes the crucial pivot point in dependent origination (paṭicca samuppāda). When we don't see sense objects, consciousness, and contact as they actually are, we become inflamed by indulgence, leading to the buildup of the five aggregates (khandha) affected by clinging and perpetuating the cycle of becoming.

Bhante explains how Right Awareness transforms this process, leading naturally to the complete Noble Eightfold Path and the thirty-seven requisites for Awakening. These include the four foundations of mindfulness (satipaṭṭhāna), four right efforts, four bases of spiritual power, five spiritual faculties, and seven factors of enlightenment. The discourse culminates in understanding what must be fully known (the five aggregates), abandoned (ignorance and craving), and realized (the three characteristics and liberation).

This teaching offers both newcomers and experienced practitioners a clear map of how sensory experience either binds us through unconscious reactivity or liberates us through wise understanding and non-attachment.
